PullRequest.Title: agentHost: open, navigate, and search long chats on demand
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Opening a long chat could disconnect the relay before it displayed the first reply. The client now opens at the latest messages (up to ten completed turns, with a byte budget) rather than requesting every reply. The gutter can still list every prompt, and Find can reach older replies. Neither requires downloading the rest of the transcript in the background.

Companion protocol draft: microsoft/agent-host-protocol#620. `listChatTurns`, `readChatTurns`, and `searchChatTurns` are optional reads. They do not move the live subscription. The client uses them only when the chat advertises `historyNavigation`; without it, Find reports results for loaded messages only.

### How to review and test

Use a client and host built from this branch and a remote chat with at least 100 turns retained by the host. Pick a word that appears only in an early reply.

1. Open at the latest reply. The [opening page](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/bd56f402568548ca03957b5bd2fd8f49c475e50c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/chatHistoryView.ts#L52) is bounded; opening the [gutter](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/bd56f402568548ca03957b5bd2fd8f49c475e50c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/promptTimeline/promptTimelineModel.ts#L317) lists prompt previews, not reply bodies.
2. Select turn 45. It opens with its real neighbors: scrolling forward shows 46, **not** 90. At the edge of the [reading window](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/bd56f402568548ca03957b5bd2fd8f49c475e50c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatHistoryNavigation.ts#L115), the next page starts from the turn on screen. **Scroll to Latest** returns to the live chat.
3. While reading 45, a reply arriving from another client should not move you. Sending a new prompt from this widget returns to latest only once the send is accepted. Old rows are read-only; a truncation must not leave a deleted turn in the gutter or Find.
4. Open Find and search for the word unique to the early reply. [Choosing the match](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/bd56f402568548ca03957b5bd2fd8f49c475e50c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatFind/chatFindWidget.ts#L669) should reveal and highlight it without fetching the intervening replies.

### Verification

- Local 100-turn fixture with **45 MiB of retained reply text**: the unpaged response was 47,200,941 bytes and rejected by the relay encoder. The opening response contained turns 93–100 in 3,776,205 bytes. The entire title index was 3,929 bytes. A one-turn read returned 45, its successor was 46, and search found the only marker in reply 3 (6,023 bytes of search results across 50 pages).
- Combined Electron run of the changed test suites: **3,287 passed, 5 pending**. Client type-check, scoped lint, and full repository hygiene passed.
- The 45 MiB check exercised the host queries and relay encoder offline. The new gutter and Find still need a human pass over a live relay, including keyboard and screen-reader testing. A fixture that generates replies only when paging cannot validate host-side Find.

### Limits

The transcript remains virtualized. Manually visited neighboring pages are kept until another jump or return to latest; this is not a fixed-size cache. Opening the gutter builds all title rows. Search reports incomplete results if it hits the worker time or concurrency limit. This change does not raise the relay limit or change authentication.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The cursor stores the same turn index plus a skip count, but every continuation rebuilds its batch and calls countMatches before using skip. The widget traverses pages serially up to 9,999 results. Exact process-startup duration is unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Worker subprocesses, serialized child-process IPC text, Markdown tokenization, and regex match-counting CPU.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For M matches in one turn and batch size B, the UI performs ceil(min(M, 9999)/100) serial worker launches and approximately that many B-sized scans/transfers. At least 10,000 hits produce 100 launches for essentially the same batch. The global four-worker limit bounds simultaneous workers, not this repetition.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sustained host CPU/allocation pressure and cumulative process-startup overhead delay completion of Find and contend with other chats.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Find searched the loaded transcript locally; there was no host search continuation, worker fork, or transcript transfer over child-process IPC.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A continuation within one matching turn launches another worker, transfers that turn and neighboring batch text again, and repeats Markdown parsing and all match counting just to return the next 100 locators.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new search calls countMatches(params, batch) on every page (line 185), while its limit branch returns a cursor for the current turn (line 196). Resumed skip is used only after the whole batch has been scanned again.
Findings.Title: Reuse scanned counts when a search page ends within a turn
Findings.Impact: Searching a common word or character in a large retained reply repeatedly forks and rescans the same text, even with warm host state. Initial local hits can appear promptly, but whole-chat traversal remains unnecessarily expensive.
Findings.Evidence: chatHistoryQueries.ts:170–185 rebuilds the batch from cursor.index without accounting for skip; line 190 applies skip only when emitting results. countMatches forks at line 74, sends full batch text at line 87, and kills the worker at line 94. chatHistorySearchWorker.ts counts all request/Markdown matches. ChatFindWidget._readHistoryMatches traverses sequential 100-hit pages until its 9,999-hit cap; no scanned-count cache exists.
Findings.Recommendation: Carry or retain bounded counts for an unfinished scanned batch, scoped to query, flags, and history revision, invalidating on revision or subscription changes. Serve within-batch continuations without launching another scanner.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The old plaintext helper explicitly truncates input at 100,000 characters. The new helper calls marked.lexer on the entire string, and history-identified segments bypass MAX_SEGMENT_SCAN. The widget invokes recompute synchronously on query changes and its 200-ms content debounce; exact stall duration is unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer-thread Markdown tokens, regex execution, match objects, and history-location allocations.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each recompute processes all B characters and M matches of a reached history reply rather than the previously capped prefix. Multi-megabyte replies are allowed by the paging budget; query changes and continued streaming repeat this work, with content updates debounced at 200 ms.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Long main-thread tasks and GC pressure block input, painting, and scrolling while Find is open.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Response plaintext extraction truncated Markdown to 100,000 characters before parsing; segment matching also stopped after 100,000 occurrences.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Agent Host replies receive historyPartId, so local Find lexes their entire Markdown and enumerates every matching occurrence synchronously, despite retaining only 9,999 results.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added historyPartId branch replaces renderAsPlaintext(part.content, FIND_PLAINTEXT_OPTIONS) with markdownToPlainText(part.content.value), whose new implementation has no input cap. chatFindModel.ts:141 also makes the former 100,000-match limit conditional on the absence of a history identity.
Findings.Title: Keep uncapped history text processing off the UI thread
Findings.Impact: Opening Find or changing its query in an Agent Host chat containing a multi-megabyte Markdown reply can freeze the workbench. A byte-bounded page still permits a large individual reply, so transcript virtualization does not bound this local scan.
Findings.Evidence: markdownRenderer.ts:861–865 bounds renderAsPlaintext input at 100,000 characters. New base/common/markdown.ts:90–91 lexes the entire Markdown string. stateToProgressAdapter.ts supplies historyPartId for retained and active replies. chatFindModel.ts:123–143 performs uncapped matching for those segments, including match/location allocations; ChatFindWidget.ts:336–338 recomputes on the renderer thread after the 200-ms content debounce.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve full-history occurrence semantics by moving plaintext extraction and match enumeration to cancellable background work, or cooperatively slicing them with a bounded UI-thread budget. Do not bypass the existing parsing and scan safeguards in synchronous recompute.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The attachment hook reaches a synchronous loop that fetches all intervening subscription pages before prompt dispatch. Relay publication eagerly serializes/enqueues pages, has a 64-MiB aggregate limit, and disposes the lane on send failure. Attachment resolution uses authoritative host turns, not the client window.
Findings.PerformanceResource: History JSON serialization, relay chunk/base64 frames, queued outbound bytes, and client history models.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For an already-subscribed source with H hidden turns between its tail and the pin, enough byte/count-bounded pages are emitted to cover all H turns. Repeated references share the expanded source window, but the first old pin can enqueue tens of megabytes in one event-loop turn. ACKs cannot drain the queue during that loop.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Bulk serialization and transfer delay prompt submission; sufficiently large suffixes overflow the aggregate relay publish queue and disconnect the client.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Sending a pinned chat attachment issued no history-page notifications. The source transcript was resolved on the host by AgentSideEffects; client openings had already received the full snapshot.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: With the short source subscription, an older pinned attachment synchronously downloads the entire intervening source suffix into the client before the prompt is dispatched, although no source-chat reducer operation needs those turns.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new _loadChatAttachmentTurns invokes _loadReferencedTurn for attachment.endTurn. Added dispatch handling calls it before _agentService.dispatchAction. _loadReferencedTurn loops at lines 4806–4812, sending pages until the old pin lies in the subscribed suffix.
Findings.Title: Avoid draining the source transcript for a pinned chat attachment
Findings.Impact: Reuse a pinned reference to an early turn after its source chat has accumulated a long transcript and is open at latest. Sending the prompt triggers an unsolicited download of later source replies, potentially exhausting the 64-MiB relay queue even though every page meets the message-size budget.
Findings.Evidence: ProtocolServerHandler.ts:3217–3218 invokes attachment hydration before dispatchAction; lines 4786–4812 synchronously generate and send every preceding page to the pin. Paged subscriptions disable channel flow control at line 2460, so AgentHostConnectionChannels.send forwards directly to transport. MissionControlLane.send and _publish eagerly serialize pages; _enqueue rejects aggregate queued/in-flight bytes above 64 MiB, and send disposes the lane on failure. AgentSideEffects.ts:2554–2563 already resolves pinned attachment text from authoritative source turns independently of client views.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not expand a source subscription merely to resolve a chat attachment; use the existing authoritative attachment-resolution path. Keep genuinely required reducer hydration separate and paced with relay backpressure, rather than synchronously draining all pages.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Relay chat subscriptions requested an unbounded completed-turn snapshot. The host sent the full retained transcript through relay JSON/chunk encoding, whose 32-MiB reassembly ceiling rejects sufficiently long chats after allocating/serializing the payload.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening a chat with more than 32 MiB of retained response JSON cannot deliver its opening snapshot over the relay, while smaller long chats incur full-history transfer and restoration latency.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The client now requests a ten-turn relay view. ChatHistoryView constructs a normally 4-MiB tail with a hard transport ceiling before the final response is serialized; older turns are transferred only through explicit reads/pages.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base request option at agentHostProtocolClient.ts:2158 supplied only bypassReconnectGate, with no history view. Blame identifies the commit carrying that request. Added line 2261 supplies view.turns=10 for WebPubSub chat subscriptions. ProtocolServerHandler._pagedChatBaseline replaces completed turns with the bounded ChatHistoryView.baseline result; chunking.ts:113–117 proves the existing 32-MiB rejection. Existing provider restoration remains unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an existing Agent Host chat at latest, including cold provider restoration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Subscription authentication and any existing session/chat restoration must finish, followed by snapshot projection, relay delivery, cooperative history replay, and widget attachment. Gutter outline loading is asynchronous and does not gate transcript publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read session registration/catalog and normalized persisted chat state when restoring a cold session/chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One restore per distinct cold session/chat after in-flight coalescing, containing multiple registration/catalog/provider reads; not one restore per displayed turn. Warm resident state avoids restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full host-side state restoration happened before serving an unpaged snapshot; this PR does not change its read cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and receive the chat subscription snapshot over WebPubSub; local/nonrelay clients use their existing IPC/socket state delivery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opening subscription per chat. WebPubSub now requests at most ten completed turns, normally within 4 MiB, with a hard 32-MiB transport ceiling and the existing active-state envelope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscription boundary transferred every retained completed turn over the relay, potentially exceeding the 32-MiB encoder ceiling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot delivery gates the first displayed response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure candidate turn JSON, then serialize, encode and chunk the bounded snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only tail candidates up to the requested turn count plus a budget-rejected candidate are measured, followed by final response encoding; the authoritative transcript is not all encoded for a paged baseline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-candidate page measurement; final relay encoding serialized the complete transcript.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Retained transcript bytes/turns, current active-state bytes, and number of independently opened cold chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One restore per session/chat key, with independent keys able to run concurrently. Cooperative client replay yields between mutations. Opening title queries are off the publication critical path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host resident snapshots are reused; session restores share _restoreSessionInFlight and restored chat resolution shares entry.inFlight. Failed resolution remains retryable. Paging reduces client transfer, not authoritative host restoration. Client subscription ownership already coalesces the logical subscription.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: client view hint, host baseline projection, byte budgeting, and encoder ceiling are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider restoration duration and actual response sizes vary; no runtime timings were collected.
Scenarios.Verdict: Opening transfer is a concrete performance improvement, submitted as an internal regression-fix signal. No separate opening-path regression found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconnect or renew authentication with several chat subscriptions and a pending prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Handshake/replay or fresh snapshots, authentication renewal, pending-turn verification, and subscription restoration precede releasing the reconnect gate/outbox.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect handshake, individually restore excluded chat subscriptions, and explicitly fetch older pages to verify an omitted pending prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one paged relay chat participates in the handshake. Remaining distinct chats are subscribed individually. Pending-turn recovery visits at most eight distinct cursors, stopping once acceptance/non-delivery can be established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconnect could combine full histories in one handshake, with no paged pending-turn lookback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Verification and restoration are awaited before normal reconnect completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure replay actions/handshake JSON and fall back to bounded baselines when necessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Replay scan stops after exceeding its 4-MiB budget; one projected handshake is checked against the transport ceiling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replay/handshake histories were not protected by these chat-specific byte checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the handshake is sent.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct subscribed chats and distance between a pending prompt's prior known turn and the new tail, after subscription deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The preferred chat is handled separately in the handshake. Other restored resources follow the existing restore workflow; a pending prompt's page verification is serial, bounded to eight pages and 30-second per-request timeouts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A received private page/cursor survives valid replay. Missed private delivery, changed history, or authorization requires a new baseline. Recovery tracks visited cursors and excludes queued unsent prompts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed bounded recovery and handshake cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A slow relay can still delay recovery, but the work is bounded and required to avoid ambiguous prompt delivery.
Scenarios.Verdict: Intentional bounded delivery-verification tradeoff; no additional high-confidence regression. Old multi-history relay overflow is mitigated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create the gutter outline, open its flyout, and display prompt headings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating the gutter starts a background outline traversal. Complete index receipt is required for the full heading list, but not for reading the opening tail. Opening/hovering the flyout synchronously creates heading rows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List visible prompt previews from retained in-memory turns through protocol requests; local clients use IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately ceil(N/100) serial pages for N eligible prompts, adjusted by response-byte budget. Hidden/system prompts are skipped without fetching reply bodies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The gutter derived all headings from the already-downloaded full transcript, with no dedicated title-index requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off transcript-opening critical path; the full outline appears after traversal finishes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eligible visible prompt count N; heading rows are not capped, while resting dots are sampled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One coalesced serial index traversal per model/source; no per-heading remote reads. DOM rows are constructed synchronously only when the flyout is revealed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Navigation stores one outline, including empty successful results. The model coalesces an in-flight outline read. Rebind/truncation replaces the navigation source and cancels traversal; conflict restarts at most once. Row construction is deferred until reveal and row listeners are disposed on replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lightweight preview-only reads and lazy rows are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large outline DOM construction can remain costly, but the old gutter also created all rows and did so eagerly; prevalence and duration are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable new regression: dedicated preview traffic replaces full-history transfer, and hidden row creation is reduced. File-change lookups remain limited to loaded prompts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Jump directly to an old turn, page its neighbors by gesture, and return to latest
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One readChatTurns response and detached cooperative replay must complete before revealing an unloaded anchor. Edge gestures await one adjacent page. Returning to latest disposes detached pages and displays the existing live model without a history fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a contiguous byte-bounded turn window around/before/after an anchor through network or local IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded query per uncached jump or adjacent edge gesture, default ten turns and normally 4 MiB. No intervening pages are downloaded for a jump. Already-visible anchors need no read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All turns were already downloaded/restored before navigation; there were no independent window requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Read/replay gates the requested reveal; does not gate ongoing live streaming.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Project and measure only window candidates, followed by final response transport encoding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded page candidates plus one rejected budget candidate, with an O(total retained turns) in-memory anchor lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening encoded all turns, rather than encoding a requested window.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Retained turns for the anchor lookup; bytes/turns in manually visited pages for client retention and list updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active edge read per navigation; list gestures are coalesced to an animation frame and in-flight load. New jumps cancel superseded reads, although an already-sent host request can finish. History mutation replay is cooperatively sliced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current-window anchors are reused; an unrelated jump clears old pages. Adjacent visited pages remain until another jump, return-to-latest, or disposal. Detached models disable background keepalive and never attach an editing session. mapObservableArrayCached disposes cached row ownership when observation/window ownership ends.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded direct reads, cancellation ownership, and absence of per-turn I/O in detached replay.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Long manual traversals retain all visited pages, but this is demand-driven and prior opening retained the entire transcript.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression in window loading/cleanup. The local Find scan over these windows is accounted for separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search retained history with a dense common query or a rare early-reply marker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Local loaded matches can appear first. Complete remote results require serial search-page responses; a chosen unloaded match additionally awaits one direct window read, not intermediate response pages.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch pages of match locators from retained host history, via network or local IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 100 locators per result page, capped by the widget at 9,999 remote matches. A sparse/no-match scan advances through batches of at most 256 turns and normally 1 MiB of text; a within-turn result continuation stays on the same turn. One conflict restart is allowed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Find scanned loaded client text only and made no host search requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial responses gate completion of whole-history search, not initial local results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fork an isolated Node search worker for each search response, wait for counts, SIGKILL it, and await closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fresh worker per page. A turn with at least 10,000 hits causes 100 serial launches before the 9,999-hit UI cap. A sparse search launches one worker per scanned batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every remote page awaits worker startup/counting/shutdown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize/send raw request and Markdown batch text to the child, parse Markdown, count all matches, and return small counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Full batch text is sent on every page, even when cursor.skip resumes within a previously scanned turn. Dense-query cost is B times ceil(min(M,9999)/100) for the repeated batch B and match count M.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No worker IPC text transfer or repeated host counting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Counts must return before the next locator page is generated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective visible request/Markdown bytes after hidden/filter exclusion, retained-turn batch count, and match density after the 9,999-result UI cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pages are serial per widget traversal. A module-global limit permits four active workers across clients; each is killed and its close awaited before releasing the slot. This is repeated startup/scanning, not a 100-worker concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host state is already resident due to subscription. Authenticated cursors store revision/index/skip but no match counts, so warm within-turn continuations rescan. Query/source identity coalesces a widget's existing traversal; closing/changing Find cancels further pages, but an already-running worker remains bounded by its time budget.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: cursor and skip placement, fork lifecycle, IPC serialization, and widget traversal are fully traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Process startup and parsing durations vary. Dense-match prevalence is unknown, but common words/characters in large generated replies are realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported repeated rescanning and subprocess/IPC work for within-turn continuations. The needed initial scan for previously unloaded history itself is not reported as a regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use local Find while a large reply is displayed or continues streaming
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous ChatFindModel.recompute must finish before query handling/result publication can proceed and before the renderer can paint or handle additional input.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Entire reached history-marked Markdown strings and their matching occurrences, including multi-megabyte single replies permitted by page limits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Main-thread synchronous lexing and matching; a 200-ms debounce coalesces content events but does not time-slice a recompute. Background host workers do not protect this separate local path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visible VM arrays are cached, but extracted plaintext/segment matches are rebuilt on each recompute. The live secondary model is empty outside history reading. Query keys coalesce remote traversal, not local parsing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: replaced helper had a 100,000-character cap, new lexer has none, matching drops its cap for history identities, and callbacks are synchronous.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual lexer and regex durations depend on text structure and query; no benchmark numbers are assumed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported loss of UI-thread parsing/matching bounds. Virtualized DOM and the 9,999-retained-match cap do not bound the work before those caps.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a pinned chat reference to an early source turn, including source-based createChat/resume hydration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: New pre-dispatch hydration serializes/enqueues source-history pages before AgentService can accept the prompt or start creating the requested chat. Downstream attachment text is still resolved from authoritative host state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Push unsolicited ChatTurnsLoaded pages to expand an already-subscribed source suffix back to the old pin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Enough pages to cover every hidden turn from the live boundary to the pin. Page count is constrained individually by view count/bytes, not bounded across the loop. Multiple pins to the same source reuse its expanded boundary; effective fan-out is per distinct source and earliest needed pin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No source-history page notifications on attachment submission; the host resolved source turns itself, and client openings received full state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All pages are generated/enqueued before new prompt dispatch; ordered outbound pages also compete with subsequent notifications/responses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure history JSON, eagerly encode relay chunk/base64 frames, and retain queued/in-flight frames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All source-suffix bytes to the pin are encoded in one event-loop turn, notwithstanding normally 4-MiB pages. Aggregate relay queue/in-flight admission is 64 MiB and 512 frames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prompt path encoded no intervening source-history pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Encoding blocks host progress; queue overflow throws and disposes the lane.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct already-subscribed pinned source chats, distance from their short tails to old pins, and intervening reply bytes after same-source grouping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous while-loop generation with no await/backpressure yield. Relay transport limits actual in-flight publishes/bytes, but pending ACK callbacks cannot execute during the loop, so the queue—not wire parallelism—absorbs the burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only active paged subscriptions with hidden turns enter the helper. Resident authoritative turns do not avoid the new client hydration. Once the source is expanded, later pins inside it incur no additional pages. Reopening/rebaselining can restore a short tail.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: pre-dispatch hook, loop, disabled paged channel flow control, eager encoder, queue limits, lane disposal, and authoritative attachment resolution are traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of old pinned references is unknown; long-lived pins and large source transcripts are realistic. Queue failure depends on source byte size and other outstanding traffic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported unnecessary source-suffix bulk transfer and queue pressure for chat attachments. Required reducer hydration ordering is acknowledged; its scheduling must be bounded separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a checkpoint after older history is prepended and keep live streaming independent of a reading window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkpoint edit resolution, review preparation, and ordered filesystem mutations finish before checkpoint position updates. Restoring the first displayed checkpoint may first await one preceding history page to identify its predecessor. Remote appends continue into the live model without seeking the reading window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch one preceding subscription page when the disabled checkpoint begins at a partial-window boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one predecessor page on this newly guarded boundary path, not all intervening history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No predecessor fetch; the client previously had full history.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read snapshot/current file contents and write/delete/move affected files for crossed checkpoints.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing operations per crossed checkpoint/file edit; equal current content avoids writes. Merely adding older checkpoint IDs performs no filesystem operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same crossed-edit file operations and ordering were present.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Crossed checkpoints and their file edits, not every title in the full outline; older-page insertion changes index positions but not existing crossing cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Undo/redo is sequenced per controller. Crossed edit resolution uses existing Promise.all; checkpoints are mutated in order and file edits within a checkpoint use the existing settled parallel operations. Predecessor page fetch is singular and awaited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved checkpoint edits are retained with turnEditsResolved; prepending IDs deduplicates against existing checkpoints and does not eagerly resolve older edits. Reading-page models are read-only and do not attach editing sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code adjusts index ownership and bounded predecessor acquisition without increasing filesystem fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote filesystem latency and edits per checkpoint vary; these costs are unchanged and were not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance regression. New predecessor lookup is a bounded ordering/correctness requirement, and existing filesystem costs are not expanded into findings.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass over all 62 changed files and every diff continuation. Submitted three high-confidence findings: uncapped renderer-thread Find processing, pinned-source hydration burst, and repeated host-search continuation scans. Submitted one internal bounded-opening regression-fix signal with base-line blame provenance. Traced cold/warm subscription, reconnect, outline, direct navigation, Find, pinned-reference send, and checkpoint scenarios; excluded correctness-only observations and pre-existing costs. Static read-only review; no code or runtime execution. The supporting guide fetch was tool-truncated; loaded skill instructions and learned mechanism guidance remained available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
